title: Pflege u. Weiterentwicklung d. GEO-Fachanwendungen für d. hessische Landwirtschaftsförderung
description: Die Wirtschafts- und Infrastrukturbank Hessen (WIBank) fungiert als von der EU-akkreditierte Zahlstelle für die Landwirtschaftsförderung in Hessen. Die WIBank ist Teil der Landesbank Hessen – Thüringen (Helaba). Die Bereitstellung und der Betrieb der für die Landwirtschaftsförderung notwendigen spezialisierten IT-Systeme liegt in der Verantwortung der Helaba. Die Helaba hat die IT-Dienstleistungen für die Landwirtschaftsförderung derzeit an einen Generalunternehmer vergeben. Der Vertrag mit diesem Generalunternehmer endet zum 31.12.2026. Daher werden die IT-Dienstleistungen neu ausgeschrieben. Im Rahmen dieser Ausschreibungen erfolgt ein Wechsel vom heutigen Generalunternehmermodell auf ein Multi-Provider-Modell. Die bisher zentral vom Generalunternehmer erbrachten Leistungen werden dabei aufgeteilt und über sechs fachlich abgegrenzte Lose sukzessive im Wettbewerb ausgeschrieben. Die IT-Systeme der Landwirtschaftsförderung basieren auf einer hochgradig integrierten Architektur, die technische und fachliche Abhängigkeiten zwischen den sechs Losen bedingt. Im Rahmen der Umstellung vom einem Generalunternehmer auf ein Multi-Provider-Modell ist es daher zwingend erforderlich, dass die Dienstleister je Los, nicht isoliert agieren, sondern Teil eines integrierten IT-Ökosystems werden. Vorliegend betroffen sind allein die Leistungen zu Los 2 - Pflege und Weiterentwicklung der zentralen GEO-Fachanwendungen für die hessische Landwirtschafsförderung. Wesentliche Bestandteile sind die Flächenverwaltung (FIG) als rechtsverbindliches Referenzsystem, das satellitengestützte Flächenmonitoring (AMS) zur automatisierten Kontrolle von Förderanträgen sowie mobile Anwendungen für Landwirte (HeLaWi-App) und Prüfdienste (HeKTAR). Der Dienstleister verantwortet die Integration von Geodaten, die Analyse von Satellitenbildern sowie die Sicherstellung der EU-Konformität und technischen Zukunftsfähigkeit der Systeme. Sämtliche Leistungen sind auf Grundlage einer Rahmenvereinbarung und mithin erst auf gesonderten Abruf/Einzelauftrag hin zu erbringen. Für die weiteren Einzelheiten wird auf die Anlage I 02 - Anlage 0_Leistungsbeschreibung verwiesen.

title: Germany – Shipping operations – Preliminary Market Consultation – Compact SOV / Walk-to-Work offshore logistics and accommodation concept for the operation and maintenance (O&M) of the ONAS offshore substation platforms in the German Baltic Sea
description: 50Hertz Transmission GmbH, acting as a utility contracting entity, is conducting a non-binding Preliminary Market Consultation pursuant to Section 26 SektVO. The purpose of this consultation is to explore whether, and under which operational and commercial conditions, a compact SOV-based (Service Operation Vessel) or Walk-to-Work (W2W) offshore logistics and accommodation concept could support the continuous operation and maintenance (O&M) of the offshore grid connection platforms (ONAS) in the German Baltic Sea. The consultation is intended to inform potential future procurement decisions. 50Hertz is interested in practical market solutions, indicative commercial logic and the main assumptions underlying such information. No offers, binding prices, detailed cost breakdowns or internal calculation models are requested. As an indicative size reference, a concept with approximately 30–50 persons on board (POB), DP2 capability, suitable W2W access to OSS interfaces, platform supply capability and Baltic Sea operability is being considered. This indication is for orientation only and does not constitute a preferred design, a preferred supplier or a mandatory technical specification. The market consultation pursues, in particular, the following objectives: Identifying the current market offering of compact, fit-for-purpose SOV / W2W concepts for continuous Baltic Sea O&M operations, as well as larger market-available SOV / CSOV tonnage. Assessing the technical feasibility of DP2 capability, W2W access up to approximately Hs 2.5 m, platform supply, transfer of fluids (diesel, oil, fresh water, grey water, waste water) and crane interfaces with the OSS. Understanding realistic market routes (newbuild, conversion, existing tonnage, shared use, campaign, winter, seasonal or back-charter models) and their associated lead times and availability drivers. Exploring the main commercial cost drivers and meaningful contractual and remuneration models. Exploring available and emerging propulsion, energy and emissions-reduction concepts, including Baltic Sea-specific framework conditions. Assessing whether such a concept can be economically implemented for the planned scope (9 relevant ONAS platforms, max. 24–48 POB per platform, approximately 3,000–10,000 person-days of offshore work per year, distributed over four campaigns).

title: ULTRA DEEP SUB-MICRON INTERFACE AND SYSTEM-IN-PACKAGE TECHNOLOGY - RE-ISSUE
description: To develop, industrialise and perform ESCC evaluation of the European highspeed interfaces for the Ultra Deep Sub-Micron Processors and FPGAs in a System in Package (SiP).The electrical power available in space is a precious resource and sets bounds on the functionality and performance realisable in spacecrafts. Advances in semiconductor technology over years have been able to push these boundaries further afield for Telecommunications, Earth-observation,Exploration and Science missions. Thanks to ESA, EC and national funding FPGA Brave Family and GR7xx microprocessors have been successfully developed using 65nm and 28nm technologies. New technologies (e.g. N7 or Finfet 7nm) have much to offer to the next generation of devices and wouldtarget a fourfold increase in digital gate density, power efficiency and highspeed serial line communication speed. Indeed, the 112Gbps high-speed serial interface cannot be realised on the FDSOI 28/22nm technology.The increasing cost and complexity of the advanced technology necessitates to leverage the existing Intellectual Property (IP) core functional blocks to the fullest extent. Only moving those functions that benefit significantly from a port and/or enhancement to the new technology should be considered. Specifically, the digital logic and high-speed serial interfaces are prime candidates. Slower and higher voltage as well as analog functionality should remain in the FDSOI 28/22nm, where cost of their port does not weight up against the accrued benefit.This approach, also known as chiplet architecture, uses a low-latency low power die-to-die interface on an organic substrate to link the different dies in the current technologies (FDSOI 28/22nm) and most advanced technologies (N7 and below). This chiplet architecture paradigm allows a larger number of components to be realised through reuse, scalability and the addition of new chiplets. As a result, the total system development cost and time to market for a component is significantly reduced. The practical implementation of this chiplet architecture approach in suitable packages will also be the objective of the activities defined in the technology line UDMS of the GSTP EEE Component Initiative.This activity aims to develop the High Speed Serial Interface up to 112Gbps in Finfet technology (N7 or below) and to demonstrate compatibility with optical transceivers at 112Gbps with SiP technologies. The activity is divided into 4 phases.The aim of the first phase is to consolidate the selection of requirements for the interfaces and Ultra Deep Sub-Micron (UDSM) technology (node N7 and below), as well as Multi-Chip Module (MCM) System in Package (SiP), wherein these will be validated and ESCC evaluated. The UDSM interfaces required by the telecom processor, microprocessor and FPGA are Double Data Rate (DDR) memory interfaces, the die-to-die (D2D) interface, 112Gbps High Speed Serial Interface (HSSL) supporting both 400G Ethernet and PCIe up to Gen 5 and additional UDSM supporting functionality. The collective is henceforth referred to as the UDSM Interface library. Furthermore, the requirements will be determined for the SiP component representative of the UDSM FPGA or processors containing these interfaces.Environmental operational conditions will be defined for the interface library elements and package. Where already existing, the interfaces will be electrically, and radiation tested to assess the degree of technology maturity and radiation mitigation necessary. License conditions for the use of the European UDSM interface technology in space components for all consortiummembers shall be agreed upon as well as access to the UDSM foundation and platform library. Alignment with future customers technical and commercial requirements shall be ensured. The demonstrator chip for UDSM interface library and SiP package to be ESCC evaluated will be defined, representative of future processors, domain specific accelerators and/or FPGAs in the UDSM technology.In the second phase the interface library elements will be developed with emphasis on low power consumption and operation in space. Due regard shall be given to their future integration into telecom processors, microprocessors and FPGA with proper pinout layout, IP and package models. The interfaces will be integrated into the demonstrators chips to ensure comprehensivevalidation with at least a representative future processor, domain specific accelerator and/or FPGA. Where necessary test chips shall be manufactured to de-risk the silicon design as well as its operation in the selected SiP package and on a Printed Circuit Board (PCB). Design validation with the test chips as well as performance analysis in the laboratory will be performed to ensure that future implementations will meet performance and functionality requirements.Radiation mitigation techniques for the selected UDSM technology shall be established and verified either by simulation or by radiation testing. The MCM SiP package to contain the demonstration integrated circuit will be designed that ensures complete electrical validation of the interface library elements and further compatibility testing with electro-optical transceivers. The accompanying PCBs will facilitate the validation testing, electrical as well as environmental and provide a demonstration board for the technology.In the third phase the UDSM interface library elements will be manufactured on a demonstration chip. The MCM SiP package will be manufactured and assembled with the demonstration chip(s) together with PCB to enable electrical validation as well as compatibility testing with electro-optical transceivers. Environmental testing will be performed to verify correct operation in the representative space environment. The signal transmission performance will be measured and characterised with suitable electrical equipment. Where necessary improvements to the design will be implemented and provided for manufacture and testing such that the final version of the design can be demonstrated to work inside current and/or future UDSM processor and FPGA.In the fourth phase the component, consisting of the SiP package containing the demonstrator chips, will be ESCC evaluated to establish the perimeter for which future products containing these interfaces and packages can be ESCC qualified.This activity will benefit from synergies with other activities of the GSTP EEE Component (e.g. SiP qualification, co-packaged optics).The 4-phases activity encompasses the following tasks:Phase 1: Specification and Initial Validation of UDSM Interface and SiP Technology- Consolidation of application, commercial and development needs as well as constraints (time to market, license for technology and IP access, quality, package availability, ...), technical specificatis, manufacturing, validation and ESCC evaluation requirements- Consolidation of the requirements for UDSM interfaces and MCM SiP package, including a flow down from all the application use cases- Determination of the demonstrator chips and SiP requirement specification- Feasibility analysis of technical requirements with technology trade-off, risk analysis including development and commercial needs and constraints (time to market, cost, license agreements, package availability, ) leading to a develop plan with smart decision gates for the activity phases and consortium organisation with commercial and licensing arrangement- Review of the interface application cases- Review available package implementation options- Review of the demonstrator chips and SiP requirement specification- Develop plan for each of the interfaces and controllers (DDR, HSSL, D2D, ..) as well as additional supporting UDSM functionality including design, validation, demonstration, future implementation and ESCC evaluation- Develop plan for the MCM SiP package including design, validation, demonstration, future implement

title: OPPORTUNITIES ARISING FROM NEW AND IMPENDING REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS - PHASE 2 (ARTES FPE 1A.110) - EXPRO+
description: The first phase of this activity comprised a review of new regulations (both under discussion and development as well as in the process of being enacted) with the goal of identifying how they might generate future opportunities for new satcom services and applications. A domain of significant potential identified through this review was the anticipated growth in remote operations for applications within fields such as the transportation, energy, and medical sectors. Such safety critical functions will require communications services across wide service regions, often beyond existing terrestrial communications infrastructure, and possibly employing diverse delivery technologies to ensure exceptionally high availability, if they are to be licensed. This second phase of the project will therefore seek to define the technical performance characteristics of the satellite communications services needed to support the most promising markets for such future remote operations.
